existing_content: Tītus, Tītī, Tītō, Tītum (781 lines in 71 tracked files)
problem: The praenomen Titus has a short i. Every occurrence marks it long.
proposed_correction: Titus, Titī, Titō, Titum (change only the first vowel; keep all other macrons)
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. Titus: 'Tĭtus, i, m., a Roman prænomen'. Collatinus lemmes.la: 'Tĭtus'. Metre: Martial 1.17.1 'Cogit me Titus actitare causas' and 1.17.3 'Res magna est, Tite, quam facit colonus' (Phalaecean hendecasyllables, Ti in a short position); Martial 7.59.1 'Non cenat sine apro noster, Tite, Caecilianus' (dactylic hexameter, 'ter Ti te' = dactyl). A&G §108.c (praenomen abbreviations) marks Mārcus, Gāius, Lūcius, Pūblius long but prints 'T. — Titus' unmarked; A&G marks all vowels known to be long (§10 end).
learner_impact: Learners memorise a wrong vowel length in the most frequent proper name (129 pilot tokens); TTS input for 9 Chapter II–VIII recordings used 'Tītus', so those takes may carry a long [iː].

existing_content: Vir et fēmina nōn in hortō sunt: vir in hortō est, fēmina in vīllā.
